summary: # Marvelous Designer Learning Day - Protective Clothing Production ## Introduction Hello everyone, I am Jimmy from Marvelous Designer. Today I will show you how to make a protective case. It looks like this. In this video, I will explain how to use the hard surface model to interact with the clothing. I will mainly introduce this part of the content. This is a video I recorded before, and I will explain it to you one by one. ## Importing the Model First, I will import the model in Marvelous Designer. Then we can adjust it in the virtual model editor. I will adjust the model size in the virtual model editor to make the model stronger and stronger. After that, I will delete the hair and shoes of the virtual model. Next, I will import a mask that I made in advance. You can see that the model of this mask has a hollow line and a protruding part. The surface of the mask is not flat or smooth, which will cause a problem. When the mask is imitated on the surface, there will be some unstable situations. There are two solutions at this time: 1. Choose a mask and increase the surface diameter of the mask. 2. Make a collision object for the mask. This is the method I recommend. Use a collision object to wrap the mask, ensuring a smooth surface, which will make your makeup more stable around it. We can reduce its transparency to observe the mask inside. When making this mask, you need to ensure that it fits your internal model. ## Drawing the Protective Mask Now, I will start to import a background image here. Based on this background image, I will draw a protective mask. Here, I will use a multilayer tool to draw. Then, I will measure the length of the sleeve. When I make clothes, I will make sure that the length of the sleeve is not too large. Next, I will add a center point here and ensure that the center point of this panel is in the right place. After adjustment, I will align the panel and arrange the panel on the virtual model. The center point of this panel is on the virtual model. While arranging, we can notice that this panel is a little bit different from the virtual model. When arranging the panel, we need to pay attention not to let the panel be too different from the virtual model. If there are too many differences, a large part of the panel will not be easy to adjust in the future. At this time, you can adjust the position of the panel in the digital editor or the 3D window. This will solve the problem of this difference. Then, perform the following sewing and modeling operations. ## Sewing and Modeling Operations Now, you can see that this clothing is worn on the virtual model. Here, I will activate the sleeve panel and arrange it in the arm position. When sewing, I can start sewing from the center point to the two ends, ensuring that the two ends are almost the same length. When sewing the sleeve, ensure that the seam line of the sleeve is down, hidden in an invisible position. This is the seam line of the sleeve, and I will make it down. The seam line of the sleeve is also down. Next, I will activate the panel of the hat, arrange it on the head, and then sew them together. Here, we can notice that the two panels on the left and right are separated. I want to merge them, so I will remove this seam line in the middle. Before merging, I need to flatten and straighten this panel. We can choose the seam line to merge. Now you can see that the seam line in the middle is eliminated, forming a whole panel. Then I will add some curves to its part to make it smoother. ## Adjusting the Inner Lines Next, I will set two inner lines on the shoulder. This inner line is mainly similar to a hemline. You can see that after I set the inner line, this inner line is not aligned. In this case, I will usually cut it off. After cutting the seam line, I will adjust it again so that they can be aligned one by one. Then, I will turn it over, and you can see that the panel can be aligned now. I will delete the panel in the middle, aligning it with the hemline. Next, I will connect this hat with the bottom clothing as a whole. Before connecting, I will freeze the bottom clothing first to prevent it from slipping. Then, I will adjust its hat panel to make the whole hat bigger. ## Final Adjustments and Details Then I will adjust the curve at the back of the hat to match the curve of the outline of the hat. After adjusting, I will sew them together. As you can see, after sewing, the hat is not wrinkled; it looks smooth. At this point, I can make some wrinkles by making the hat bigger. I will give the hat a woolen pattern. When using the woolen pattern, the whole hat will be bigger and a little harder. At this point, we can notice that there is a gap between the model and the panel. We can select the model we have inserted and reduce its surface diameter. This will make the gap between them smaller. I will align the front and center lines and absorb the middle line. On this side, I will align the front and center lines. As you can see, the curve is not smooth. We need to adjust its curve at this point. ## Additional Steps Now, I will adjust the surface geometry and knock on the model. Then, I will not merge it up in front of it to eliminate the shadow effect in the 3D window. I will carve out a layer of this envelope and increase the thickness of the rendering so that it becomes thicker and forms an envelope. Next, we will apply a layer mask to ensure that it can maintain the original version of the shape and not produce stretching or deformation. I will now deal with the sleeve part. On the sleeve side, I will set up an inner line to make its sleeve. After we cut the sleeve out, I will adjust the size of the sleeve to be a little smaller. Then, we will freeze the sleeve and lengthen the sleeve sheet separately. After adding the sleeve, if you're in the model, we will have those folds stacked in the sleeve. Then we come to the crotch area, which is not a very neat line. If we want it to be more level and neat, I will choose a 3D drawing tool in the 3D window and build a level line on the board. In the 2D window, we can find the position of the drawing of this line. We can use the inner line tool in the 2D window to cut the seam line after the inner line is made. ## Creating Wrinkles and Finalizing the Model Of course, you can also choose the line you just drew in the 3D window and cut the seam line directly. After we cut it, we can get a neat crotch. Here, I'm going to lengthen the sleeve sheet a little bit. I will also create a crotch similar to the way the hand was made. The side of the sleeve is almost the same, with a little downforce here to get it closer to the model's legs for the shoes. You can also use the cologne layer to the outside of the board and freeze it to the inside. You can see that I've extended this side and lengthened this side in the 2D window, changing the shape in the 3D window. Now, we will have to make some creases. There’s a question about the creases in the middle of the waist and a lot in the crotch area. If I want to keep the creases in the crotch area while adding some to the waist, I will add an inner line to the waist. After cutting it down, we will lengthen the waist piece separately. This way, we can keep the creases in the bottom of the pants better without recalculating the simulation. ## Conclusion This is the part of the demonstration for today.
